messages:
sara-support: FYI Acme sent an escalation — their Dedicated pool (eu-west-2) is seeing repeated 504s and huge tail latencies on /v1/generate. They say p95 ~400ms normally, p99 hitting 2s+ during bursts. Errors look like 504 gateway/timeouts and occasional 429s. Starts around 2026-03-17T09:12Z. Can someone triage?

priya-sre: Can you paste the pool id + a couple request ids and the approximate time window? Also useful: node names and MIG profile for the pool.

dan-customer: Pool ID: dp-eu2-47. Sample request IDs: rq_8a7f2b, rq_8a7f9c. Time window: 2026-03-17T09:10:00Z — 09:25:00Z. Observed SM util ~95% and memory-bandwidth near 99% on the host GPU when it spikes. We're running mixed batch workloads (inference + reranking).

rick-eng: Thanks. Two quick asks: 1) any recent changes to MIG partitioning or autoscaler config? 2) are there other tenants on the same hosts?

dan-customer: No config changes from our side. We are on a Dedicated pool but not single-tenant hosts (we have reserved MIG slices). We did start a nightly batch-run yesterday that ramps to 200 concurrent requests.

priya-sre: Ok. Please run these on one of the affected nodes and attach outputs:
```
# node shell
kubectl get pods -n redwood --selector=pool=dp-eu2-47 -o wide
kubectl top pod -n redwood --containers
kubectl describe node <node-name>
# gpu probes
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,mig.mode.current,mig.devices,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,clocks.sm --format=csv
nvidia-smi dmon -s u
```
Also collect /var/log/redwood/serving.log around the time window and the redis enqueue queue length (we've seen queueing preceding 504).

sara-support: Attached snippet from serving.log (09:14:22):
```
[09:14:22.312] WARN enqueue_delay=128ms queue_len=146 worker_wait=70ms route=/v1/generate model=rw-instruct-large
[09:14:22.313] ERROR request_timeout id=rq_8a7f9c status=504
```

rick-eng: Those enqueue_delay signs + very high queue_len + high SM util suggest noisy neighbor contention — likely cross-MIG resource pressure (L2/L3/memory bandwidth) on the host. Not classic CPU-sched; it's GPU-level.

priya-sre: Can you also run a lightweight microbench to confirm bandwidth saturation? e.g. from the node:
```
# run synthetic kernel to saturate or test
python3 bench/bench_mem_bw.py --duration 60
# or run a short iperf between containers to rule out NIC as cause
iperf3 -c <peer> -t 30
```
If bench_mem_bw pushes mem bw near 100% and correlates with enqueue spikes we have confirmation.

maya-accounts: Heads-up — if we need to bump the pool to single-tenant hosts that will affect billing (reserved capacity + migration). Customer flagged they might need predictable latency; want us to propose mitigation options before proposing costy changes.

rick-eng: Mitigations (ordered by invasiveness):
- Short-term: schedule their critical routes onto lower-concurrency replicas (reduce batch size or per-request concurrency) and increase autoscaler min nodes to spread MIG slices.
- Mid-term: anti-affinity so their MIG instances don't share a physical host with noisy tenants.
- Longer-term: move them to single-tenant hosts or dedicated GPUs.

priya-sre: Technical note: mixed MIG profiles on the same physical GPU can cause cross-slice contention for memory subsystem and L3 cache causing unpredictable tail latency. We saw this pattern before with mixed 1g and 7g slices. Check MIG config:
```
nvidia-smi mig -lgip
# or
nvidia-smi mig -lgi
```

dan-customer: I ran nvidia-smi earlier — output shows some nodes with: 1g.10gb + 7g.40gb slices on same physical gpu.

sara-support: I kicked off a diagnostic agent. deploy-bot: any trace link?

deploy-bot: Diagnostic run completed for dp-eu2-47. Trace: https://internal.traces/redwood/diag/1845678901 (internal). Collected: nvidia-smi, dmon, serving.log, redis-qlen, kernel dmesg.

rick-eng: Looking at the trace: during the 09:12-09:16 window we see sustained SM util 92-98% on slice owners, mem bw saturation, and periodic L3 eviction bursts. Host-level perf counters show mem_write_bytes high. This lines up with noisy neighbor.

priya-sre: Proposed immediate action steps for support runbook:
1) Add a temporary scheduling rule: set kube pod anti-affinity for pool dp-eu2-47 against label redwood.noise_experiment=high.
2) Limit concurrency per replica: env RW_MAX_CONCURRENCY=64 for the time being.
3) Increase autoscaler min nodes from 2 -> 4 for dp-eu2-47 to spread load.
4) If spikes persist after 2 hours, create migration plan to single-tenant host.

maya-accounts: I'll draft an email with cost/options for single-tenant vs anti-affinity.

dan-customer: We'll try lowering concurrency and run the bench script. Expect to report back in ~45m. Thanks. :thumbsup:

sara-support: One more repro idea if you can run it: hit the API with a steady stream at your daytime p95 QPS but with synthetic input that forces longer decode (seq=1024) to amplify kernel memory. Command:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"x"*1024}' & done
```
Watch dmon and enqueue.

rick-eng: If customer agrees to test a targeted move we can run a short migration during low-traffic window and validate tail p99 before/after. We'll capture perf counters to show delta.

dan-customer: Running bench now. Will push logs to the trace link.

priya-sre: Thanks everyone. Keeping this open — if we confirm mem bw saturation correlated with queue spikes we'll mark as noisy-neighbor; recommend anti-affinity + autoscale bump as interim fix.

sara-support: closing loop: agreed plan: customer lowers concurrency + run bench; we apply anti-affinity + raise min nodes if bench reproduces. If no improvement, schedule single-tenant migration.

dan-customer: Update: bench showed mem bw 98% and enqueue_delay jumps to 140ms under same QPS. Will accept anti-affinity change.

sara-support: Noted. @maya-accounts we'll proceed with interim mitigation and monitor.

rick-eng: Recording follow-ups: 1) Create infra ticket to detect mixed MIG profiles on same host and alert (Action: infra/monitoring). 2) Add a scheduler policy template for per-customer anti-affinity. 3) Run a post-mortem if migration needed.

priya-sre: Adding a quick grep snippet to find mixed MIG profiles across nodes: 
```
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name); do ssh $n "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=gpu_name,mig.devices --format=csv"; done | grep -E "1g|7g|3g" -n
```

sara-support: Thanks team. Dan — ping here when the anti-affinity test is done and we'll verify p99. :pray:
